pr_title: Fix: Fixed an issue with drag and dropping items onto .py files
pr_body:
Allow for python files to be treated as executable files in order to allow dragging and dropping other files onto them. 
Two main things changed were adding python to the executable files list, and not allowing for python files to be ran through Launcher.LaunchFileAsync() because when it does, it does not pass in the parameter, and returns true. Which means it will not run Win32Helpers.InvokeWin32ComponentAsync(), which runs the python file witht he proper path parameter.

issue_context.title: Bug: Unable to drag and drop any file onto .py files
issue_context.body:
### Description

The drag-and-drop functionality seems to have a limitation, preventing the dragging and dropping of files with any file extension onto .py files.

This does not happen with .bat.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Make a .py file
2. Try to drag any file onto it.

### Requirements

It should allow me to drag and drop file onto .py files, but it currently does not.

### Files Version

3.0.5.0

### Windows Version

10.0.22631.2506

### Log File


[debug.log](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/13360569/debug.log)
comments: Thanks for the report, I've added this to the project board.
I think this is custom behavior we had to add for batch files but I assume the same can be done for .py.
Got a fix going, will try to submit a PR tomorrow morning!
Let's work on support for a single file first and once that's merged, we can take a look at the behavior for multiple files.
